title: Min-K% Membership Signal as a Lightweight Contamination Flag

original_idea.body:
# Min-K% Membership Signal as a Lightweight Contamination Flag

**Problem:** A success state requires detecting which specific benchmark items a model has memorized. A needed result is a runnable, documented Min-K%-probability contamination flag for open models that a beginner can apply.

**Direction:** Implement the Min-K% probability method on an open model: compute average log-prob of the lowest-k% tokens for each benchmark item, and compare the distribution against held-out fresh items of matched difficulty. Items with anomalously high membership scores are flagged. Deliverable: a reusable script and a contamination flag-list for one benchmark.

**Why it matters:** Memorized items inflate scores and hide true (un)safety. Min-K% needs only token log-probs from an open model - no canary access, no training, no lab data. Gives the community a turnkey contamination check. Counterfactual and reusable.

**Relevant context:** Survey arXiv 2502.17521 documents Min-K% probability as a detection method; awesome-data-contamination list (GitHub lyy1994); contamination listed as open in International AI Safety Report 2026.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (contamination flagging improves score trust) but indirect to catastrophic risk; tooling.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing Min-K% needs token log-probs and some care matching difficulty; guidable for novice+mentor.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: implement Min-K%, compare vs fresh items, flag-list + script.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: No canary/lab access, turnkey tool; reusable but largely re-implementing a known method.

low_compute.reasoning: Token log-probs from open model, inference-only.

novelty.reasoning: Min-K% is an established published contamination detector; re-implementation is largely addressed.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Min-K% is a documented existing method.
